findings.reason: Untrusted source: rf_num_slots is a 16-bit field of struct rcom_config sent by a remote DLM cluster node over the DLM recovery protocol (the peer endpoint of a network cluster protocol, the analogue of the seed's remote usbip peer). The peer message is copied verbatim into the shared, persistent lockspace object ls->ls_recover_buf by receive_sync_reply() (fs/dlm/rcom.c:266 'memcpy(ls->ls_recover_buf, rc_in, rc_in->rc_header.h_length);'), allocated kmalloc(dlm_config.ci_buffer_size) at fs/dlm/lockspace.c:586; upstream length validation in midcomms.c:78-101 checks only h_length (msglen <= ci_buffer_size and msglen <= actually received len) and never bounds the number of embedded rcom_slot records against it. dlm_recover_members() (fs/dlm/recover.c:207) calls dlm_slots_copy_in() after wait_status_low(), consuming the shared peer-populated buffer. Poisoning store: member.c:118 copies num_slots = le16_to_cpu(rf->rf_num_slots) with the only validation being 'if (!num_slots) return -1' - no maximum check, no cross-check against the peer-supplied h_length or the locally known ci_buffer_size. Missing guarantee / asymmetric validation: the sibling path of the same protocol, dlm_slots_assign() (member.c:166), enforces a local maximum before sending slots out - 'max_slots = (dlm_config.ci_buffer_size - sizeof(struct dlm_rcom) - sizeof(struct rcom_config)) / sizeof(struct rcom_slot); if (num > max_slots) ... kfree(array); return -1;' (member.c:276-281) - but the copy_in/receive mirror path applies no such clamp, exactly the seed's submit-vs-return asymmetry. Unsafe use: the loop at member.c:124-127 walks ro0 for num_slots iterations (each struct rcom_slot is 16 bytes, dlm_internal.h:487-492) and performs an in-place read-modify-write 'ro->ro_nodeid = le32_to_cpu(ro->ro_nodeid); ro->ro_slot = le16_to_cpu(ro->ro_slot);' - with num_slots up to 65535 this runs up to ~1MB past the ls_recover_buf heap allocation, an OOB read+write of peer-supplied-adjacent heap; log_slots() (member.c:63-95) is called at member.c:129 with the same unclamped num_slots and dereferences the same ro0 walk, and the second matching loop at member.c:132-134 reads every slot again. Error-unwind facet: the early returns at member.c:141-144 ('our slot changed') and member.c:152-155 ('no slot') leave ls->ls_generation already updated from the peer value (member.c:117 'ls->ls_generation = gen;') and member slots partially populated from the OOB walk, so the failed iteration poisons lockspace recovery state that later recovery stages consume. Counterevidence checked: h_length itself is bounds-checked (midcomms.c:91-94), so the OOB requires the peer to send rf_num_slots larger than the slot records its h_length actually carried (the message-length check validates the declared length, not the embedded count) - a malicious or buggy cluster peer can do this at any time recovery is awaited, making this the error/reply-direction consumption of a peer-controlled count with no local maximum.

candidates.reason: Seed mechanism present verbatim and unpatched in s02: usbip_pack_pdu(RET_SUBMIT, unpack) stores 'urb->number_of_packets = rpdu->number_of_packets;' (line 392) with no clamp, USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS does not appear anywhere in drivers/usb/usbip of this snapshot (enforced only implicitly by stub_rx submit-side checks), usbip_recv_xbuff/usbip_recv_iso consume it, and vhci_rx.c:80-88 returns to usb_hcd_giveback_urb (line 99) with the poisoned count. Excluded from reporting per the seed-never-reportable rule; recorded so a later worker can decide snapshot-local seed presence (consistent with the treatment in facts f004/f005/f008/f015).

dlm_slots_assign (TX side) enforces the local maximum before the slots array is serialized: 'max_slots = (dlm_config.ci_buffer_size - sizeof(struct dlm_rcom) - sizeof(struct rcom_config)) / sizeof(struct rcom_slot); if (num > max_slots) ... return -1;' (member.c:276-281). This is the enforcing sibling path proving the asymmetric validation, not itself vulnerable.

receive_sync_reply memcpy(ls->ls_recover_buf, rc_in, rc_in->rc_header.h_length) copies the peer recovery message into shared persistent lockspace state; h_length is validated (midcomms.c:81-101) but the embedded rf_num_slots/rcom_slot payload it announces is never cross-checked against it, so the unclamped count is what dlm_slots_copy_in later iterates. Part of the reported finding.

midcomms_process_incoming_buffer validates msglen = le16_to_cpu(p->header.h_length) against sizeof(struct dlm_rcom), dlm_config.ci_buffer_size (line 91-94) and the actually received len (line 100) before dlm_receive_buffer; header-length validation present, but it validates only the declared total length and never the embedded slot count - the gap exploited by the reported finding.
dlm_recover_members() non-low-nodeid branch calls dlm_slots_copy_in(ls) right after wait_status_low(), consuming the peer-populated ls_recover_buf; part of the reported finding's consumption chain.

num_logops = be32_to_cpu(rhead->h_num_logops) from the on-disk log header; located by the wire/disk count-store sweep but its error paths and consuming loops were not deep-read before the finalize directive.

*num_of_nodes = le16_to_cpu(rsp->NumberOfReferrals) from the DFS server reply with no maximum clamp observed at the store; downstream kcalloc/consumers and error unwinds not deep-read before finalize.
fwcfg->num_uf_bufs = be16_to_cpu(fwcfg->num_uf_bufs) from firmware config reply feeds bfa_uf_res_recfg and bfa_svc.c:5456 memory sizing; error/teardown iteration paths not deep-read before finalize.

NAPI_GRO_CB(skb)->count = le16_to_cpu(cqe->num_of_coalesced_segs) is the standard GRO metadata byte count consumed by GRO stack min_t clamps; not an error-unwind iteration of an unvalidated count, and the value crosses into standard skb bookkeeping whose consumers bound by skb length.

pend = &urb->iso_frame_desc[urb->number_of_packets] walk uses number_of_packets assigned by the same driver from locally computed num_packets (allocation-matched); not peer-controlled, no poisoned count (all non-usbip number_of_packets consumers in s02 assign the field locally before allocation - btusb.c:929, bas-gigaset.c:900/985/1017, hfcsusb.c:958, media drivers - spot-checked).

vldb->nr_servers loop bounds located by the object-count sweep (afs volume/vl_probe/vl_rotate iterate nr_servers set during VLDB reply decode); the decode-side clamp and error unwinds were not deep-read before finalize.

limitations: The sweep was bounded by the finalize directive: high-signal queries covered number_of_packets consumers across drivers/net/fs/block, wire/device count stores (le/be*_to_cpu, get_unaligned, nla_get) across the tree, and object-field iteration loops (->num/->nr/->count/->nents/->len); deep reads covered fs/dlm (member.c, rcom.c, midcomms.c, lockspace.c, recover.c) and drivers/usb/usbip (seed, excluded by rule). Error-unwind poisoning patterns in other naming conventions (iovec teardown, vring abort paths, scsi command teardown) were only enumerated, not exhaustively audited.

The reported DLM finding's OOB requires a malicious or buggy cluster peer to send rf_num_slots exceeding the rcom_slot records actually carried in the validated h_length; the header-length check (midcomms.c:91-101) bounds the message, not the embedded count, so the invariant violation (validated length, unvalidated count, no local maximum on the receive mirror while the transmit sibling enforces max_slots) holds, but no runtime reproducer was built (read-only snapshot; DLM recovery requires a multi-node cluster).

Unresolved candidates fs/xfs/xfs_log_recover.c:4616 (h_num_logops), fs/cifs/misc.c:676 (NumberOfReferrals), drivers/scsi/bfa/bfa_core.c:1298 (num_uf_bufs), fs/afs nr_servers decoders, and the seed-verbatim usbip stores (excluded by rule) were located but not fully walked to their consuming loops and error unwinds before the finalize budget.

All conclusions come from direct source reading (grep/sed) of the read-only snapshot; no compilation, static analyzer, or runtime harness was run, and line numbers for the dlm_slots_assign max_slots check (member.c:276-281) were counted from the sed window at member.c:135-300.
